units.title: Osnove
units.theme: Everyday greetings, self-introduction, numbers, colors, and family vocabulary for absolute beginners.

skills.title: Pozdravi
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian distinguishes informal address (ti) from formal or plural address (vi): 'Kako si?' (asking one person you're informal with) vs 'Kako ste?' (formal, or speaking to more than one person).

skills.title: Predstavljanje
skills.grammarFocus: Present tense of 'biti' (to be): ja sam, ti si, on/ona/ono je, mi smo, vi ste, oni/one su.

skills.title: Brojevi 1-10
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian numbers change the case of the noun that follows: 'jedan' (one) agrees in gender with the noun; 2-4 take the noun in genitive singular ('dva stola' - two tables); 5 and above take the noun in genitive plural ('pet stolova' - five tables).

skills.title: Boje
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian adjectives — including colors — agree in gender with the noun they describe: 'crven auto' (red car, masculine), 'crvena jabuka' (red apple, feminine), 'crveno cvijeće' (red flowers, neuter).

skills.title: Porodica
skills.grammarFocus: Possessive pronouns agree in gender with the noun they modify: 'moj brat' (my brother, masculine), 'moja sestra' (my sister, feminine), 'moje dijete' (my child, neuter).
